arxiv-2012-04551.title: CoShaRP: A Convex Program for Single-shot Tomographic Shape Sensing The paper is under consideration at Pattern Recognition Letters
arxiv-2012-04551.creator: Ajinkya Kadu, Tristan van Leeuwen, K. Joost Batenburg, [2ex] Computational Imaging, Centrum Wiskunde & Informatica, Amsterdam, The Netherlands
arxiv-2012-04551.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Ajinkya Kadu, Tristan van Leeuwen, K. Joost Batenburg, [2ex] Computational Imaging, Centrum Wiskunde & Informatica, Amsterdam, The Netherlands. We introduce single-shot X-ray tomography that aims to estimate the target image from a single cone-beam projection measurement. This linear inverse problem is extremely under-determined since the measurements are far fewer than the number of unknowns. Moreover, it is more challenging than conventional tomography where a sufficiently large number of projection angles forms the measurements, allowing for a simple inversion process.

arxiv-2402-05708.title: On the role of parametrization in models with a misspecified nuisance component Thanks: Department of Mathematics, Imperial College London, 180 Queen’s Gate, London SW7 2AZ, UK. Thanks: Department of Statistical Sciences, University of Toronto, 700 University Ave, 9th Floor, Toronto, Ontario M5G 1Z5
arxiv-2402-05708.creator: H. S. Battey, N. Reid
arxiv-2402-05708.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by H. S. Battey, N. Reid. The paper is concerned with inference for a parameter of interest in models that share a common interpretation for that parameter but that may differ appreciably in other respects. We study the general structure of models under which the maximum likelihood estimator of the parameter of interest is consistent under arbitrary misspecification of the nuisance part of the model.

arxiv-2406-08286.title: Copy-composition for Probabilistic Graphical Models
arxiv-2406-08286.creator: Toby St Clere Smithe
arxiv-2406-08286.description: Abstract In probabilistic modelling, joint distributions are often of more interest than their marginals, but the standard composition of stochastic channels is defined by marginalization. Recently, the notion of ‘copy-composition’ was introduced in order to circumvent this problem and express the chain rule of the relative entropy fibrationally, but while that goal was achieved, copy-composition lacked a satisfactory origin story.

arxiv-2408-10955.title: Multichannel Attention Networks with Ensembled Transfer Learning to Recognize Bangla Handwritten Charecter
arxiv-2408-10955.creator: Farhanul Haque, Md. Al-Hasan, Sumaiya Tabssum Mou, Abu Saleh Musa Miah*, Jungpil Shin*, Md Abdur Rahim
arxiv-2408-10955.description: Abstract The Bengali language is the 5th most spoken native and 7th most spoken language in the world, and Bengali handwritten character recognition has attracted researchers for decades. However, other languages such as English, Arabic, Turkey, and Chinese character recognition have contributed significantly to developing handwriting recognition systems.

arxiv-2503-04840.title: Framing the Game: A Generative Approach to Contextual LLM Evaluation
arxiv-2503-04840.creator: Isaac Robinson *, John Burden †
arxiv-2503-04840.description: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed across diverse contexts to support decision-making. While existing evaluations effectively probe latent model capabilities, they often overlook the impact of context framing on perceived rational decision-making. In this study, we introduce a novel evaluation framework that systematically varies evaluation instances across key features and procedurally generates vignettes to create highly varied scenarios.

arxiv-2503-11518.title: Future collider constraints on top-quark operators
arxiv-2503-11518.creator: Fernando Cornet-Gomez, Víctor Miralles, Marcos Miralles López, María Moreno Llácer, Marcel Vos
arxiv-2503-11518.description: Abstract In this paper we present updated constraints on the top-quark sector of the Standard Model Effective Field Theory using data available from Tevatron, LEP and the LHC. Bounds are obtained for the Wilson coefficients from a global fit including the relevant two-fermion operators, four-quark operators and two-quark two-lepton operators.

arxiv-2505-21289.title: LoFT: Lo w-Rank Adaptation That Behaves Like F ull Fine- T uning
arxiv-2505-21289.creator: Nurbek Tastan, Stefanos Laskaridis, Martin Takáč, Karthik Nandakumar, Samuel Horváth
arxiv-2505-21289.description: Abstract Large pre-trained models are commonly adapted to downstream tasks using parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods such as Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA), which injects small trainable low-rank matrices instead of updating all weights. While LoRA dramatically reduces trainable parameters with little overhead, it can still underperform full fine-tuning in accuracy and often converges more slowly.

pmc-10550624.title: Incidence of malignancies after lung transplantation and their effect on the outcome. 26 years' experience
pmc-10550624.creator: Konstantina Spetsotaki, Achim Koch, Christian Taube, Dirk Theegarten, Markus Kamler, Nikolaus Pizanis
pmc-10550624.description: BackgroundMalignancy is a significant, life-limiting complication after lung transplantation (LuTx) and the second common long-term cause of death. We aimed to investigate its incidence and effect on the outcome.MethodsThis is a retrospective observational study. Between 1996 and 2022, n = 627 lung transplantations (LuTx) were performed in our department.

pmc-11508066.title: Genome of Russian Snow-White Chicken Reveals Genetic Features Associated with Adaptations to Cold and Diseases
pmc-11508066.creator: Ivan S Yevshin, Elena I Shagimardanova, Anna S Ryabova, Sergey S Pintus, Fedor A Kolpakov, Oleg A Gusev, Brad Freking
pmc-11508066.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Russian Snow White (RSW) chickens are characterized by high egg production, extreme resistance to low temperatures, disease resistance, and by the snow-white color of the day-old chicks. Studying the genome of this unique chicken breed will reveal its evolutionary history and help to understand the molecular genetic mechanisms underlying the unique characteristics of this breed, which will open new breeding opportunities and support future studies.

pmc-11654039.title: Impaired sensitivity to thyroid hormones is associated with all-cause and cause-specific mortality among chronic kidney disease patients: results from National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) 2007–2012
pmc-11654039.creator: Chan Liu, Xiaoxiao Zhu, Dingding Wang, Naya Huang, Wei Chen
pmc-11654039.description: BackgroundResistance to thyroid hormone shows underlying mechanical link with chronic kidney disease (CKD) and is prevalent in CKD population. However, whether it attributes to mortality risk among CKD population is unknown. This study aimed to examine the association of thyroid hormone resistance (THR) with all-cause and cause-specific mortality among CKD individuals.

pmc-11803451.title: Sensor-controlled fertigation management for higher yield and quality in greenhouse hydroponic strawberries
pmc-11803451.creator: George Kerrigan Hutchinson, Lan Xuan Nguyen, Zilfina Rubio Ames, Krishna Nemali, Rhuanito Soranz Ferrarezi
pmc-11803451.description: Controlled environment agriculture (CEA) for strawberry (Fragaria x ananassa) production has experienced a growth in popularity in recent years, particularly in North America. One of the most common growing systems in CEA strawberry production is the soilless hydroponic system, which uses an inert substrate and nutrient solution to grow the plants.

pmc-12457769.title: Understanding the Impact of Individual Nucleotide on Oxford Nanopore Current Signals With Interpretable Prediction Models
pmc-12457769.creator: Yenan Wang, Zhixing Wu, Jia Meng
pmc-12457769.description: Oxford nanopore sequencing enabled real-time, long-read analysis of DNA by detecting ionic current signals associated with K-mer sequences. Although many studies analyzed sequence and modification detection, our understanding of how multiple nucleotides of the K-mer sequence determine nanopore signals together is still limited. In this study, we seek to unveil the positional impact of individual nucleotide through interpretable prediction models.

pmc-12717175.title: A Chromosome-level genome assembly of the black ant Formica fusca
pmc-12717175.creator: Hao Chen, Shuo Jin, Zicen Li, Haonan Duanmu, Chenghao Huang, Jing Liang, Runguo Shu, Fei Li, Shuping Wang, Kang He
pmc-12717175.description: Formica fusca is an ideal model organism for investigating social behaviour and chemical communication in insects. Here, we present the first high-quality chromosome-level genome assembly of F. fusca, generated using PacBio HiFi sequencing and Hi-C scaffolding technologies. The resulting genome assembly spans 535.26 Mb, is anchored to 27 chromosomes, and achieves a scaffold N50 of 20.27 Mb.

pmc-12736857.title: Development and Experimental Validation of an Integrated Evaluation Framework for EMS Smartwear Electrodes
pmc-12736857.creator: Gihyun Lee, Uri Chae, Jungmin Yun, Donghyeon Seo, Inyoung Jang, Geunho Ham, Taehoon Kim, Hongbum Kim, Marco Caruso
pmc-12736857.description: This study presents an integrated evaluation framework for textile-based electrical muscle stimulation smartwear electrodes, combining physiological and user-centered assessments to ensure comprehensive performance analysis. Four electrode types—lock stitch, knit, hot stamping, and moss stitch—were examined using a systematic five-step process with nine participants.

pmc-13078015.title: Comparison of echocardiography and surgical pathology in pediatric cardiac tumor with follow-up: a single-center retrospective study
pmc-13078015.creator: Xuechen Liu, Mengqi Zhao, Lianyi Wang
pmc-13078015.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundAlthough cardiac tumor in children are clinically rare, they present significant diagnostic challenges. This study aims to characterize the echocardiographic features of pediatric cardiac tumor and to correlate these findings with surgical and pathological results, thereby improving diagnostic accuracy.

pmc-13115776.title: Maternal PTSD and Depression as Predictors of Child Internalizing and Externalizing Symptoms: The Mediating Roles of Parenting Stress and Maternal Mentalization
pmc-13115776.creator: Rossella Procaccia, Giulia Segre, Cristina Liviana Caldiroli
pmc-13115776.description: Background: Exposure to intimate partner violence (IPV) represents a major risk factor for both maternal psychological well-being and child development. Maternal psychopathology—particularly depression and post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD)—has been shown to impair parenting functioning and increase children’s vulnerability to emotional and behavioral difficulties.

pmc-13315183.title: Integrating 16S rRNA gene sequencing and transcriptomics to investigate the hepatoprotective effects of compound Ilicis Rotundae Cortex against lipopolysaccharide / enrofloxacin-induced liver injury in chicks
pmc-13315183.creator: Geyin Zhang, Zhidan Zhang, Jian Meng, Yajing Qian, Yuxi Qin, Zhuoran Li, Shiqi Luo, Yuxin Li, Jieyu Su, Hongbin Si
pmc-13315183.description: Compound Ilicis Rotundae Cortex (CIRC) has been demonstrated to ameliorate E. coli-induced liver injury. However, its efficacy and regulatory mechanisms against liver injury in chicks remain unclear. In this study, a chick liver injury model was established using lipopolysaccharide (LPS) and enrofloxacin (ENR) to investigate the effects of CIRC.
